subject: bandicoot
title: This Animal Is Pregnant for Just 12 Days, the Shortest of Any Mammal

scenes.text: This animal is pregnant for twelve and a half days.
The bandicoot, a rabbit-sized marsupial from Australia. Gestation: 12 and a half days. An elephant takes 22 months.
The newborn weighs about 0.2 grams, a fifth of a paperclip. It crawls into a pouch that opens backwards and clamps onto a teat.
For about 55 days the pouch does what the womb didn't. Then the young are out, and the mother can breed again.
The strange part: most marsupials barely have a placenta. Bandicoots grow a true one, like ours. It just only has a few days to work.
Mature at three months, litters all year round. Twelve and a half days.

description:
A bandicoot is pregnant for about 12.5 days, the shortest gestation recorded for any mammal.
The long-nosed, northern brown and eastern barred bandicoots all give birth after roughly 12.5 days. The newborns weigh about 0.2 grams and crawl into a rear-opening pouch, where they stay for around 55 days. Unusually for marsupials, bandicoots form a chorioallantoic placenta similar to that of placental mammals, but it operates for only the last few days of the pregnancy. Females mature at three to four months.
Which animal's pregnancy surprises you more: 12 days, or an elephant's 22 months?
first_comment: A bandicoot can have one to seven young per litter, usually two to four. Which animal has the longest pregnancy you know of?
